newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party plays down importance of poll.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party plays down importance of poll.

text.p: The chairman of Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) put on a brave face for reporters on Thursday after an opinion poll indicated his party's candidate would place third in a three-way race for mayor of Mexico City.
"The polls so far just reflect people's moods and naturally do not yet reflect their voting intentions," PRI chairman Humberto Roque said.

The Center of Opinion Studies at the University of Guadalajara published a poll on Wednesday showing that the conservative National Action Party's (PAN) candidate would have would have won 42.9 percent of the votes cast if an election had been held last week.
The center-left Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) would have come second with 23 percent, and the PRI in third place with 17 percent.

Recent political reforms provided for direct election of Mexico City's mayor this year. The Mexican president has directly appointed the capital's mayors since 1929, when the PRI was founded and began its unbroken occupancy of the presidency.
The PRI also faces midterm elections in the lower chamber of congress and for a quarter of seats in the Senate. Six state governorships are also up for grabs.
Roque said the opinion polls did not worry the PRI. "I believe citizens will appreciate the PAN's lack of credibility right now and the PRD's lack of consistency," he said.
